ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against SEPBLAC risk typologies and sanction lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and (EC) No 2580/2001), UN Security Council sanctions, and the OFAC SDN list as a cross-border USD clearing benchmark. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory under Ley 10/2010 arts. 4 and 14 for all politically exposed persons, shareholders, and counterparties in high-risk third countries, in particular across Latin American distribution channels; the complete EDD file must be documented before any incorporation deposit, name closing, or merchant account application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — www.rmc.es — online application for Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Spanish (Castilian) or another official language of Spain (Catalan/Balearic, Galician, Basque); it must include 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; it must not be identical or phonetically confusingly similar to any existing registered name; foreign-script or non-Latin-alphabet brand names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for inscription.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Caja, Bank — requires prior authorization of the Banco de España
Seguros, Reaseguros, Mutualidad, Fondos de Pensiones — requires prior authorization of the insurance supervisory authority
España, Estado, Gobierno, Ministerio, Administración — requires prior ministerial authorization
Organismo Oficial, Agencia, Tribunal, Consejo — implies public authority status and is rejected absent written justification
Holding, Grupo — accepted only if the underlying holding or group structure is evidenced in the by-laws
Names contrary to criminal law, public order, morality, or likely to induce error as to the corporate object
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative certification (denegatoria), the applicant may file a within-one-month administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice, attaching evidence of prior use or lawful entitlement to the rejected denomination; alternatively, the applicant may immediately resubmit an online application with up to five alternative names. A positive certification is valid for 90 days, must be attached to the public deed of incorporation within that window, and may be renewed for one successive 90-day term if the deed is still pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: No. A virtual office is not accepted as the sole statutory seat. Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (RDL 1/2010) requires the registered office to coincide with the place where the actual management is located or where the main establishment or operations are conducted. The nutraceuticals e-commerce license requires a physical address declared in the prior communication to the competent health authority and in the municipal trading license application; a virtual office can serve only as a supplementary correspondence address once a physical seat is registered and operational.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 80% within the first 18 months of operation. The high-risk nutraceutical retail classification triggers routine and risk-based inspections by AESAN (Agencia Española de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición) and regional public health authorities under Ley 17/2011 and EU Regulation 2017/625; unannounced on-site inspections of offices, storage facilities, and the e-commerce fulfilment channel are standard.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly articles 22 (minimum capital), 23 (public deed), 59 (registered office), 62 (subscription and payment of shares), 124-127 (bylaws) and 209-210 (board resolutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name reservation, and the competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for inscription of the incorporation deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución), submitted for legal inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry and subsequent publication in the Official Gazette of the Commercial Registry (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the minimum share capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution in a blocked escrow-type account in the company's name; the bank certificate must be presented to the notary, and the deposit may be released only after the Mercantile Registry inscription is obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: That the founding members approve the subscription and fully paid contribution of EUR 3,000 in cash, divided into 3,000 participating interests of EUR 1.00 each, evidenced by the bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution. RESOLVED SECOND: That the statutory registered office is hereby fixed at [Madrid address], Calle ..., to serve as the principal place of administration, and the board may establish physical or logistical premises as business requires. RESOLVED THIRD: That [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator (Administrador Unico) with all powers permitted under the Capital Companies Act, and that execution of the public deed and all registry filings is ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain certification of proposed company name (certificacion negativa de denominacion social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry electronic headquarters (Sede Electronica del Registro Mercantil Central).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application for a negative name certificate, providing up to three proposed corporate names in order of priority. The certificate reserves the chosen name for a limited statutory period and is required for execution of the public deed.
required_dossiers: Form 'Certificacion de denominacion social'
DNI, NIE, or passport copies of all founders or legal representative
Notarial or other power of attorney if filed by a third party
Proposed corporate names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused for similarity or identity with an existing name, file a fresh application with alternative proposed names; no amendments are accepted within the same refused application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification number and register with the tax agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria) through its Electronic Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before formal incorporation, file Form 036 (statutory census filing) to obtain a provisional NIF in the name of the company in formation, identifying the proposed company name and the future registered office. The provisional NIF is included in the notarial deed and is converted to a definitive NIF after Mercantile Registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Form 036, duly completed
Negative name certificate from the Central Commercial Registry
Identification documents of the future legal representative
Proposed registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax agency queries the proposed address or representative capacity, correct the requested fields and resubmit electronically; the application can be reactivated once the inconsistency is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit initial share capital and obtain bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Bank of Spain (Banco de Espana).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital subscription account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the minimum capital of EUR 3,000. Obtain a bank certificate identifying the account holder, deposit amount and date, and deliver it to the notary before signing the constitution deed. The capital must remain blocked until successful Mercantile Registry registration.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF issued in Step 2
Proposed corporate name and reservation certificate
DNI, NIE, or passport of the account signatory
AML/CFT due-diligence information required by the credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplementary customer due-diligence documents under anti-money-laundering rules, submit them without delay; alternatively, a certified bank check endorsed to the blocked account may satisfy the deposit requirement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute public incorporation deed (escritura de constitucion) before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Escribano Publico / Notaria) within the notarial district of the company's registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding partners appear personally or by authorized representative before the notary to sign the incorporation deed and approve the bylaws (estatutos), including the corporate object, registered office, share capital, administration structure, accounting closing date, and digital communication mechanisms. The notary will verify the lawfulness of the instrument and give the first and second copies, which are needed for registration.
required_dossiers: Lawyer-drafted deed and draft bylaws
Negative name certificate from Step 1
Bank certificate of capital deposit from Step 3
Provisional NIF from Step 2
DNI, NIE, or passport of each shareholder and administrator
Acceptance statement by the proposed administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the draft deed or a missing document, execute a corrective addendum or amend the bylaws and schedule a second signing date; the original will remain pending until all defects are cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry and obtain inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) corresponding to the registered office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period after notarization, submit the notarial deed and supporting documents to the Provincial Commercial Registry. The registrar examines the legality of the instrument, registers the company, and issues the certificate of inscription. The registered deed gives the company full legal personality and allows release of the block on the statutory capital deposit. The registry also transmits the relevant data for publication in BORME.
required_dossiers: Notarial first copy of the incorporation deed
Application form for commercial registration
Proof of payment of applicable registration fees
Tax form evidencing payment of transfer and stamp duty if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a negative qualification notice, the company's legal counsel must cure the defects described in the note and resubmit the documents within two months; if that period lapses, the filing must be renewed with the same or corrected deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain definitive NIF, release capital and open operational high-risk merchant accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT) for conversion of NIF; the credit institution for capital release; authorized payment institutions for merchant accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Mercantile Registry inscription, file Form 036 again to convert the provisional NIF to the definitive NIF, presenting the registry certificate of incorporation. Then present the definitive NIF to the bank to release the blocked capital. After incorporation, complete the KYC process for a high-risk merchant account and credit-card processing, providing corporate documents, legal governance information, compliance policy, and evidence of the industrial and health licenses required for the supplement e-commerce activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Mercantile Registry inscription
Notarial deed and registered bylaws
Form 036 definitive NIF application
Corporate bank release request and original deposit certificate
Beneficial-ownership declaration and identification of directors
Proposed e-commerce compliance and AML policy for merchant account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT does not issue the definitive NIF automatically, resubmit Form 036 with the registry certificate and correct any censal discrepancies; if the acquiring bank queries the high-risk business model, supply the food-supplement notification, operational licenses, and supporting compliance documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Spanish Agency for Medicines and Health Products (AEMPS) under the Ministry of Health; local competent authority (Ayuntamiento) for municipal activity and opening licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Prior communication for the placing on the market of food supplements (Comunicacion de puesta en el mercado de complementos alimenticios) and, where physical premises are used, the municipal Activity and Opening License or prior communication (Licencia de actividad y apertura / comunicacion previa de ejercicio).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (MITECO) for state-level EIA screening; competent Environment Council (Consejeria de Medio Ambiente) of the relevant Autonomous Community for regional environmental licensing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment for pure online retail and storage of packaged dietary supplements; where a physical warehouse or logistics center is installed, the activity is classified as a low-impact commercial/storage activity requiring only a municipal environmental communication or simplified environmental registration under Annex II of Law 21/2013 on environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge process is operated; if municipal sewer connection exists, wastewater must meet local municipal sanitation limits (typical interval: pH 6-9, COD less than or equal to 500 mg/L, suspended solids less than or equal to 400 mg/L). Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from packaging solvents are below the formal registration threshold of 2 tonnes per year. Waste handling must comply with Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils; hazardous waste producer registration is required if hazardous waste generation exceeds 10 kg per year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification issued by the municipal fire service or an authorized inspection body, covering detection, extinguishing, and evacuation. Structural load inspections must be performed for storage racking and mezzanine areas. An occupational risk prevention assessment and plan must be prepared in accordance with Law 31/1995, including first-aid equipment, emergency coordination, and health surveillance when six or more workers are employed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including its Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The AEAT administers Spanish corporate income tax, value added tax, tax identification numbers, the census of businesspersons and professionals, and VAT identification for intra-Community transactions. Customs matters are administered through the AEAT Customs and Excise Department.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains its tax identification number (NIF) by filing Modelo 036 with the AEAT. A provisional NIF is generally requested after incorporation using the public deed or equivalent formation documentation, articles of association, registered office details, identification of directors and shareholders, and evidence of the company's incorporation process. The definitive NIF is obtained after registration with the Mercantile Registry and submission of the registered constitutional documents. The company must register in the Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholding Agents before commencing taxable activity and must identify its economic activities and VAT obligations. The NIF normally serves as the Spanish VAT number; for intra-Community transactions and VIES purposes it is used with the prefix ES and requires registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036. A foreign entity without a Spanish permanent establishment generally applies for a Spanish NIF through Modelo 036, directly or through an authorized representative, submitting its constitutional documents, foreign tax identification evidence, proof of authority, and Spanish translations and legalization or apostille where required. A non-established business seeking Spanish VAT registration must provide evidence of the taxable activities and appoint a Spanish tax representative where required by Spanish and EU VAT rules, particularly for businesses established outside the EU.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no U.S.-style check-the-box election for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish corporate income tax as a separate legal person. Available elections or optional regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for qualifying newly created entities or qualifying small entities where statutory conditions are met, the special regime for reorganizations, the patent box regime, and VAT special regimes where the business and transaction profile qualify. Spanish anti-hybrid-mismatch rules generally apply by operation of law and are not elective. VAT grouping, cash-accounting, and other special VAT regimes require statutory eligibility and timely election or notification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), harmonized with the EU VAT system. Spanish VAT applies in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla are outside the Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general Spanish VAT turnover threshold applies. A person or entity carrying out an economic activity independently must register and comply with VAT from the commencement of taxable activity, subject to the applicable place-of-supply rules. The intra-Community VAT operator register has no general turnover threshold. Distance sales of goods to EU consumers are subject to the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold for the relevant combined intra-Community distance-sale and electronically supplied service rules, after which destination-country VAT generally applies; the One Stop Shop may be used where available. Spanish distance-selling and import rules may also require IOSS or destination-state registration depending on the transaction structure.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently impose universal real-time invoice clearance for all private-sector transactions. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires near-real-time electronic submission of VAT invoice-record data, generally within four working days, for businesses with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, entities registered in the monthly VAT refund regime, and businesses that voluntarily opt in. The electronic invoicing framework under Law 18/2022 on the Creation and Growth of Companies will require electronic invoicing for qualifying B2B transactions after its implementing rules and statutory transition periods become operative; consumer-facing obligations differ. The VERI*FACTU and related invoicing-system integrity rules require compliant software, traceability, integrity, retention, and, where applicable, secure transmission or reporting of invoice records under the applicable implementation timetable. There is no blanket requirement for a digital stamp or advance AEAT clearance on every invoice. Invoices must contain the required tax data, including supplier and customer identification, NIF where applicable, invoice number and date, taxable base, VAT rate, VAT amount, and legally required reverse-charge or exemption wording.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the supplier retains reliable evidence of export and exit. The supplier should normally be identified as exporter or otherwise prove the qualifying export transaction and link the customs exit evidence to the invoice and goods. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported there, the supplier verifies and reports the customer's VAT number, and the required recapitulative statement and transport evidence are maintained. Services supplied to business customers established outside the relevant Spanish VAT territory may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the applicable place-of-supply rule, but the treatment depends on the service category, customer status, and use-and-enjoyment rules. Dietary supplements, nutraceuticals, medicines, and medical products must also satisfy applicable EU and Spanish product, labeling, health-claim, and market-placement requirements; tax treatment cannot be determined solely from the commercial description.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration and customs Movement Reference Number (MRN), including evidence of customs release and exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the supplier, consignee, goods, quantities, values, origin, and applicable tariff classification
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, courier manifest, or equivalent carrier record
Proof of delivery or destination, where necessary to establish that the goods left the EU and to link the shipment to the invoice
Exporter's EORI number and customs authorization or representation records, where applicable
For intra-Community supplies rather than third-country exports: customer's valid EU VAT number, transport evidence, and EC Sales List or equivalent recapitulative reporting
Accounting records linking the invoice, customs declaration, inventory movement, payment record, and VAT return
Bank payment or inward-remittance evidence where commercially available; Spanish VAT law does not impose a universal inward-remittance certificate as a condition for every export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for export proceeds. Export exemption depends principally on actual dispatch or transport outside the EU and adequate documentary proof, not on repatriation of sale proceeds within a fixed period. If an exemption or zero-rating claim is unsupported, the AEAT may assess the unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, and may deny or claw back input-VAT recovery connected with the transaction. Under the General Tax Law, penalties for incorrect tax treatment commonly range from 50% of the underpaid amount for ordinary infringements to 100% for serious infringements and up to 150% for very serious infringements, subject to statutory classifications, concealment, fraudulent means, repetition, and mitigation or reduction rules. False, manipulated, or deliberately incomplete customs evidence may also trigger customs debt, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture consequences where applicable, and potentially criminal exposure for tax fraud or smuggling if statutory criminal thresholds and intent requirements are met. Refunds obtained without entitlement may be recovered with interest and sanctions. Documentation should be retained for the applicable Spanish tax limitation period, generally four years, without prejudice to longer retention periods applicable to customs, accounting, product-regulatory, or criminal matters.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and the Spanish Ministry of Economy for foreign exchange oversight
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange controls exist for residents or non-residents. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable) and reporting to the Bank of Spain for statistical purposes. Capital account transactions (e.g., foreign direct investment, loans) require post-transaction declaration via the 'Declaración de Operaciones' (D-1, D-2, D-3 forms) but no prior authorization is needed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds is imposed. Exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic or foreign accounts. However, all export transactions exceeding €12,500 (or equivalent) must be reported to the Bank of Spain within 30 days of the transaction via the 'Declaración de Operaciones de Comercio Exterior' (D-1 form). No conversion ratio applies; proceeds can be held in EUR or foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito de Capital) / Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Spain licenses Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the PSD2 framework (e.g., Bnext, Monei, or foreign EMIs with passporting rights). However, for high-risk nutraceutical e-commerce, EMIs often impose stricter due diligence and may decline due to the sector's AML risk. Legal constraints include the need for a Spanish or EU passporting license, and EMIs typically do not provide credit facilities or complex FX hedging. They are viable for operational accounts but not for capital escrow or large trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for Spanish SLs under the 'non-face-to-face' KYC procedures, provided the company and its directors pass enhanced due diligence. Directors may complete video identification (via notary or bank's digital tool) and submit apostilled corporate documents. However, for high-risk sectors, banks may require an in-person interview at a branch or a notary office, especially for the first account opening. The final decision rests with the bank's compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification (ISIC 4791 – online retail of dietary supplements) triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD) under Spanish AML Law 10/2010.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Valid pharmaceutical/nutraceutical license from the Spanish Agency for Medicines and Health Products (AEMPS) or regional authority; (2) Certificate of incorporation and tax ID (NIF); (3) Detailed business plan and source of funds declaration; (4) Beneficial ownership register (Registro de Titularidades Reales); (5) Compliance manual and AML training certificates; (6) Bank references from previous financial institutions; (7) Audited financial statements (if available).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transactions to/from high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Latin America) may trigger sanctions screening and PEP checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Commercial contracts and invoices with clear purpose codes; (2) Export/import documentation (customs declarations, bills of lading); (3) Proof of regulatory compliance in target markets (e.g., FDA, ANVISA); (4) Detailed transaction flow chart; (5) Legal opinion on sanctions exposure; (6) Enhanced due diligence on counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection (minimum capital for SL is €3,000, but higher amounts may be scrutinized).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Bank statements showing the origin of funds; (2) Notarized declaration of source of wealth; (3) Tax clearance certificate (AEAT); (4) Proof of transfer from shareholders' personal accounts; (5) If funds from foreign investors, provide foreign exchange transaction records and declaration to Bank of Spain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'G300' (equity injection) or 'G100' (direct investment). The transfer must be accompanied by a notarized capital increase resolution and filed with the Commercial Registry. For amounts above €1,000,000, a prior declaration to the Bank of Spain (D-2 form) is required. Verification includes matching the beneficiary name (SL) and NIF, and ensuring the sender is the shareholder. For non-EU transfers, additional anti-money laundering checks apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to suppliers, with purpose code 'G200' (trade payments) or 'G300' (imports). (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700 for large or recurring purchases, especially from Asia or Latin America. (3) For intra-EU payments, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is available for low-value transactions. All outbound payments must be reported to the Bank of Spain if exceeding €12,500 (D-1 form).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts (deliverable) – available for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major pairs; requires a credit line with the bank.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permissible for exotic currencies (e.g., BRL, MXN) where deliverable forwards are illiquid; typically offered by larger banks.
Currency Swaps – for long-term hedging of cross-border cash flows, subject to ISDA agreements and collateral requirements.
FX Options – available for strategic hedging, but require premium payment and are less common for SMEs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by shareholders within six months of fiscal year-end; filing within one month of approval. For 31-December year-end: accounts approved by 30 June and filed by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed administrative fine up to EUR 1,200 plus escalating penalties; closure of the registry sheet after 14 months of non-filing, preventing valid registration of corporate acts; continued default may lead to administrative removal and deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation Tax Return (Impuesto de Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months and 25 days after the end of the tax period; for 31-December year-end: due 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% depending on delay, with late-payment interest; continued failure enables AEAT compulsory collection and administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statement of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Declaración de Titulares Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry delivered together with annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the filing of annual accounts; within one month after approval. Typical due date 30 July for a 31-December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing blocks the registry sheet and other corporate filings; civil liability to the company and third parties; fines under Spanish AML law of up to EUR 10,000 for one-off breaches.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if the company meets at least two of the following in two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total exceeds EUR 2,850,000; net turnover exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Public-interest entities are always audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) as set out in the Commercial Code; consolidated groups must apply IFRS where required by EU regulation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SL is obliged to maintain an in-house Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titulares Reales) and to file an annual confirmation of that register with the Provincial Mercantile Registry when submitting annual accounts. Every share transfer or change in control must be inscribed in the internal UBO register and disclosed in the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titulares Reales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Corporate Income Tax rate for Spanish-resident companies, including an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). The rate is subject to statutory reduced-rate regimes applicable by tax year and taxpayer profile.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated companies generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules. Qualifying start-up companies under the Spanish Startups Law may also qualify for a 15% rate during the statutory period. Qualifying microenterprises and small enterprises may benefit from reduced rates, subject to annual turnover thresholds and transitional legislation. Tax depreciation, research and development deductions, investment deductions, loss utilization, double-tax relief, and regional incentives may reduce the effective rate. Dividend participation exemption may apply to qualifying corporate shareholdings, generally subject to a minimum 5% participation and a one-year holding requirement, with a statutory limitation generally reducing the exempt amount to 95%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited. Spanish tax losses may generally be carried forward without a fixed expiry period, subject to percentage utilization limits, minimum taxable income rules, anti-loss-trafficking provisions, continuity and documentation requirements. The user-specified five-year limit does not reflect current Spanish Corporate Income Tax law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, annual Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized representative. Modelo 202 is used for advance Corporate Income Tax payments. Modelo 232 is the related-party and tax-haven transactions information return where statutory thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for Modelo 200; three advance installments for Modelo 202 where applicable; annual or transaction-triggered information filing for Modelo 232.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200: within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the usual filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202: generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December, with electronic direct-debit cut-off dates usually earlier. Modelo 232: generally within the month following the ten months after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end, ordinarily 1 to 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period commencement and closing dates, legal form, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the Spanish taxpayer. The SL files under its own Spanish NIF. Foreign shareholder identity, tax residence, participation percentage, and beneficial ownership should be retained where relevant to withholding, related-party, and anti-abuse analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting result before tax based on statutory accounts prepared under the Spanish General Accounting Plan or applicable approved accounting framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent accounting figures must be reconciled to the SL's Spanish statutory accounts. Foreign exchange, intercompany charges, and overseas branch or permanent-establishment items require documented accounting treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add non-deductible expenses and deduct exempt or otherwise excluded income, including non-deductible penalties, gifts, provisions, impairment items, related-party adjustments, exempt dividends, and tax depreciation differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct foreign parent costs merely because they are charged to the SL. Charges must satisfy benefit, necessity, arm's-length pricing, allocation, and documentary requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax depreciation and amortization under statutory tables, accelerated-depreciation regimes, leasing rules, and any qualifying investment incentive.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported equipment, software, fulfillment assets, and platform costs must have ownership, useful-life, capitalization, and cross-border payment documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter available tax loss carryforwards and the amount utilized in the current period, subject to statutory utilization limits and minimum taxable income rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses cannot be transferred informally to a foreign shareholder or affiliate. Acquired loss companies and changes in ownership may trigger anti-loss-trafficking restrictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include primary, secondary, and compensating transfer-pricing adjustments where applicable, supported by local-file, master-file, benchmarking, and intercompany-agreement evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border purchases, management services, financing, royalties, marketing support, logistics, and guarantees must be reported and priced consistently with the functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base after statutory adjustments and apply the ordinary, reduced, start-up, microenterprise, or other legally available rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's residence does not itself entitle the SL to a reduced rate. Eligibility must be tested at the Spanish entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim qualifying domestic credits, research and development incentives, employment or investment credits, and relief for foreign-source income or foreign tax paid where legally available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require evidence of the foreign tax, income attribution, payment or final liability, and applicable treaty or domestic-law limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Modelo 202 installments, Spanish withholding tax, and other legally creditable prepayments against final Corporate Income Tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding suffered by the SL is not automatically a Spanish withholding credit. It must qualify under Spanish domestic law or an applicable treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the final amount payable or refundable and select the approved electronic payment, direct-debit, refund, or deferment procedure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds are paid to an account meeting AEAT requirements. Foreign bank-account details and power-of-attorney arrangements should be validated before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete balance-sheet, profit-and-loss, reserves, shareholder, related-party, tax-loss, participation, and other mandatory schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign shareholders, group relationships, ultimate beneficial ownership, cross-border transactions, and tax-haven or low-tax jurisdiction exposures accurately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notice and without tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty of EUR 100, or EUR 150 where the filing is required after a request, subject to statutory reductions. Where tax is payable and filing is voluntary before notice, the surcharge is generally 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. Where AEAT has initiated enforcement or issued a notice, a tax penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount may apply, with higher levels for aggravating conduct. Modelo 202 and Modelo 232 have separate late-filing and underpayment consequences. False data, concealed income, deliberate evasion, and obstruction may trigger criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax advance-payment form, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installment cycle: April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed and paid from the first day through the twentieth day of April, October, and December. The payment deadline may be earlier when using direct debit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's NIF, registered name, tax period, and filing period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's own NIF even where a non-resident shareholder funds the payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select electronic payment, direct debit, recognized debt, or other permitted settlement method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the payment account and authorized signatory satisfy Spanish banking and electronic-filing requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the installment using either the prior year's assessed tax method or the current-period taxable-base method, where the company is required or entitled to use the latter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Large companies may be subject to the current-period calculation method and minimum installment rules. Foreign group revenue can affect large-company status under statutory aggregation provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the amount payable after credits and legally permitted offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not offset foreign tax or unverified group payments against the Spanish installment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate statutory surcharges, late-payment interest, enforcement costs, and, where applicable, formal tax penalties. Underpayments caused by an incorrect calculation may result in an assessment and penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, subject to facts and statutory reductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, related-party and tax-haven transaction information return, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual where the statutory transaction, related-party, or tax-haven reporting thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within the month following the ten months after the end of the tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the counterparty, relationship category, transaction type, amount, currency, and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include qualifying transactions with foreign parent companies, subsidiaries, common-control entities, directors, and entities in the same consolidated group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify goods, services, financing, guarantees, royalties, leases, restructuring, or other transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify marketplace, fulfillment, procurement, marketing, licensing, and intercompany financing accurately; do not aggregate legally distinct transaction categories improperly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report transactions and holdings falling within statutory tax-haven or equivalent reporting categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enhanced review is required for payments to jurisdictions with low effective taxation, secrecy features, weak substance, or non-cooperative status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the transfer-pricing methodology and retain supporting agreements, invoices, functional analyses, and benchmarking.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing does not replace the Local File or Master File. All reported amounts must reconcile with the ledger, statutory accounts, and VAT and withholding records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or inaccurate filing may result in fixed penalties under the General Tax Law, assessment of the underlying tax, transfer-pricing adjustments, and additional penalties for documentation failures or obstruction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish company to non-residents. Domestic exemptions may apply, including the EU Parent-Subsidiary regime where the recipient and payer satisfy ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and anti-hybrid requirements. A tax treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 5%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty and participation conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Spanish payer should obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's foreign tax authority before applying a treaty-reduced rate or exemption at source. The certificate should cover the payment date or relevant tax period and be renewed when required. The payer must verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test exposure, ownership percentage, holding period, legal form, subject-to-tax status, and anti-conduit indicators. Spanish withholding is generally reported through Modelo 216 and summarized through Modelo 296. If withholding was made at the domestic rate, the non-resident recipient may generally seek a refund through Modelo 210 with residence, payment, withholding, beneficial-ownership, and treaty-entitlement evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish non-resident withholding is generally 24% for payments to residents outside the EU and European Economic Area and 19% for qualifying EU or EEA residents, subject to statutory conditions. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 5% to 10% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%, but the applicable bilateral treaty controls. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide a withholding exemption for qualifying associated EU companies meeting minimum ownership, legal-form, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, holding-period, and anti-abuse requirements. Payments to related non-residents require arm's-length pricing, treaty-benefit analysis, withholding certificates, and documentation. Spanish withholding may also apply to management, technical, digital, advertising, or other services where Spanish-source rules or a Spanish permanent-establishment analysis is relevant.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: There is no single monetary threshold that universally triggers all Spanish Local File and Master File obligations. A Local File is generally required for material related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions for certain entities and transaction categories. The principal safe-harbor threshold for not preparing related-party documentation is generally transactions with the same related party not exceeding EUR 250,000 in aggregate at arm's-length value during the tax period, subject to important exclusions and transaction-specific rules. Modelo 232 reporting may be triggered at EUR 250,000 for transactions of the same type and valuation method with the same related party, or by separate percentage and special-regime thresholds. Master File obligations generally apply to entities forming part of a qualifying multinational group, subject to statutory exemptions and size thresholds. Large multinational groups may also have Country-by-Country Reporting obligations, generally at the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other internationally accepted methods may be used where the prescribed methods are not reliable and the taxpayer demonstrates their suitability.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no standalone economic-substance regulation identical to the UAE or certain other ESR regimes. Nevertheless, substance is material under Spanish anti-abuse rules, the Principal Purpose Test in applicable treaties, beneficial-ownership requirements, the EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest and Royalties Directives, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid mismatch rules, permanent-establishment principles, and general anti-avoidance provisions. A Spanish SL should maintain real decision-making, adequate personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure, commercial risk, books and records, local management control, and evidence that cross-border arrangements have genuine business purposes. A letterbox company, conduit dividend vehicle, artificial service provider, or entity lacking control over risks may lose treaty or directive benefits and face reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and concealed revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting online sales, routing customer receipts through foreign accounts, omitting marketplace settlements, fabricating expenses, or maintaining parallel accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessment, late-payment interest, and a tax penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on concealment, fraud, repetition, and cooperation. Serious tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax period may constitute a criminal offense; aggravated fraud exceeding EUR 600,000 or involving an organization or particularly serious circumstances may attract substantially higher imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability for unpaid taxes where they caused or failed to prevent the infringement, and criminal liability where they participated knowingly. Criminal tax convictions may result in imprisonment, fines, disqualification from public benefits or subsidies, and seizure or confiscation of assets. Travel restrictions may be imposed in criminal or enforcement proceedings where legally justified; they are not automatic for every tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT fraud and carousel or missing-trader arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: False intra-EU supplies, fictitious export evidence, fraudulent input VAT claims, sham distributors, circular invoices, or deliberate misclassification of supplements and consumer products.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unduly claimed VAT, interest, administrative penalties commonly linked to the unpaid or improperly claimed amount, and possible criminal prosecution for serious VAT fraud. Customs duties, import VAT, seizure, and product-related penalties may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false VAT chains or benefit from fraudulent refunds may face joint liability, criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, asset seizure, and disqualification. Lack of knowledge is not a defense where governance failures amount to willful blindness.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold on dividends, interest, royalties, or Spanish-source service payments; applying treaty relief without a residence certificate; or failing to file Modelo 216 or Modelo 296.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, filing and payment penalties, and potential liability for the payer as withholding agent. Incorrect treaty application may also trigger interest and anti-abuse reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be secondarily liable where the company deliberately or negligently failed to withhold or remit tax. Intentional concealment or falsification may create criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially inflated imports, underpriced exports, unsupported management charges, excessive royalties, shareholder expenses booked as deductions, interest-free or overleveraged financing, or inconsistent related-party pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to taxable income, secondary adjustment, withholding consequences, interest, documentation penalties, and transfer-pricing penalties. Failure to provide documentation can generate fixed penalties and percentage-based penalties linked to the adjustment or omitted data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for knowingly approving non-arm's-length arrangements and criminal liability if the arrangements are part of deliberate tax fraud. Liability is not created solely by an unfavorable pricing outcome where contemporaneous support and reasonable methodology exist.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty shopping, and beneficial-ownership abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL as a conduit for dividends, interest, or royalties without personnel, decision-making, commercial risk, or beneficial ownership; inserting entities solely to obtain treaty or EU Directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or directive relief, withholding at the domestic rate, tax assessment, interest, anti-avoidance penalties, and possible recharacterization of payments or transactions under Spanish and treaty anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling persons may incur civil liability and, where fraud is intentional, criminal liability. Corporate separateness may be disregarded in exceptional cases of abuse, asset commingling, fraudulent undercapitalization, or use of the company to defeat creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained high-risk card payments, using opaque payment processors, structuring refunds, dealing with sanctioned persons, failing customer due diligence, or disguising beneficial ownership and source of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML penalties may be classified as minor, serious, or very serious, with substantial administrative fines, public statements, temporary restrictions, and possible loss of authorization. Criminal money-laundering conduct may result in imprisonment, fines, and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may be personally fined or prosecuted where they knowingly participate, consent, or negligently permit AML breaches. Asset freezing and travel restrictions may arise in criminal investigations or judicial proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing a supplement with unauthorized medicinal claims, selling unregistered or adulterated products, importing without required controls, breaching labeling rules, or operating without required health, food, warehouse, or distance-selling registrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, product withdrawal, recall, seizure, closure, suspension or loss of authorization, customs detention, consumer claims, and possible criminal liability for public-health offenses, fraud, or counterfeit products.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal fines, civil compensation, professional disqualification, and imprisonment for intentional or grossly negligent conduct causing public-health harm. Corporate insurance may not cover deliberate regulatory violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating tariff classification, customs value, origin, importer of record, product composition, or preferential-origin entitlement for supplements imported into Spain or the EU.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture, loss of simplified procedures, and potential anti-fraud prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable under customs and tax provisions where they directed or knowingly tolerated false declarations. Criminal liability may arise for organized or fraudulent evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends from unlawful reserves, paying shareholders while insolvent, concealing liabilities, falsifying accounts, destroying records, or continuing operations while knowingly worsening creditor losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of unlawful dividends, civil damages, director disqualification, insolvency clawback, creditor claims, accounting penalties, and possible criminal sanctions for false accounting or insolvency offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency shortfall, compensate creditors, return diverted assets, and bear litigation costs. Criminal offenses may result in imprisonment, fines, and disqualification from management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without legally required website disclosures, failing distance-selling and withdrawal obligations, using unfair subscription terms, misrepresenting health benefits, or improperly processing customer data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consumer, e-commerce, data-protection, and advertising fines; injunctions; refund and compensation claims; suspension of campaigns; and potential restrictions on processing or selling products.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for deliberate or grossly negligent violations, especially where they approve misleading health claims, conceal the seller's identity, or disregard repeated regulator notices.
